## Overview

K-nearest neighbors (KNN) predicts from the $k$ most similar training observations. In this assignment you will compute KNN by hand to see why scaling matters, then use Python to choose $k$, study what irrelevant predictors do to KNN, and compare KNN regression with LASSO.

## Problem 1 (by hand)

A car dealer wants to predict whether a customer will buy an extended warranty (Yes/No) from the customer's age and income (in thousands of dollars).

| Customer | Age | Income | Bought warranty |
|:---------|:----|:-------|:----------------|
| A        | 25  | 40     | No              |
| B        | 35  | 60     | Yes             |
| C        | 45  | 80     | Yes             |
| D        | 20  | 20     | No              |
| E        | 40  | 30     | No              |
| F        | 30  | 75     | Yes             |

A new customer is 28 years old with an income of 52. Round your answers to 3 decimals.

a.  Compute the Euclidean distance from the new customer to each of the six customers, using the raw values.

b.  Predict the new customer's class with $k = 1$ and with $k = 3$.

c.  Now apply **min-max scaling** to both predictors, $x' = \dfrac{x - \min}{\max - \min}$, using the minimum and maximum of the six training customers. Scale the new customer the same way and recompute the six distances.

d.  Predict the new customer's class again with $k = 1$ and $k = 3$.

e.  Did any prediction change? Explain why in two or three sentences.
